question_interpretation: Asks what the QMSR amendment changed in Part 820 and the date from which compliance is required.

issues.detail: The final rule is 89 FR 7496 (pages 7496-7525). 89 FR 7523 is where the revised Part 820 text begins (the CFR source note for 820.3 uses it), so it is a valid pinpoint for the Part 820 amendment, but the rule citation should be 89 FR 7496; the Part 4 conforming amendments start at 89 FR 7522.

The FR sets an effective date of February 2, 2026; there is no separate 'compliance date', though FDA states it will not require compliance before the effective date. Calling it the compliance date is acceptable.

J says FDA supplements were 'retained' at 820.10(b)-(e), 820.35 and 820.45; these are new provisions (some carry over QS-regulation requirements, e.g. 820.45 labeling controls and the 820.35(d) confidentiality clarification).

J omits that ISO 9000:2015 Clause 3 (terms and definitions) was also incorporated by reference (820.7(a), 820.3), that the part was retitled 'Quality Management System Regulation', that QS-regulation record-type terms (DMR, DHR, DHF, QSR) were eliminated, and the conforming amendments to Part 4.

H '1 through 8 (entire standard)' is internally inconsistent: FDA confirms the QMSR incorporates the entire standard including the Introduction (Clauses 0.1, 0.2, 0.4), and 820.3(b) itself relies on Clause 0.1. The standard's title in I matches 820.7(b).

explanation: The core of J is right: ISO 13485:2016 is incorporated by reference, former Subparts C-O were removed and reserved, Subpart B adds 820.35/820.45, and the QMSR applies from February 2, 2026. The key omits the ISO 9000 Clause 3 incorporation, the retitling and the elimination of DMR/DHR/DHF terminology. Its FR citation is a regulatory-text pinpoint rather than the rule citation. H's '1 through 8' range conflicts with FDA's statement that the whole standard, Introduction included, is incorporated.
proposed_corrected_answer: The QMSR final rule (89 FR 7496, Feb. 2, 2024; revised Part 820 text at 89 FR 7523-7525) revised and retitled Part 820 'Quality Management System Regulation': it incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference (820.7(b), 820.10(a)) and ISO 9000:2015 Clause 3 definitions (820.7(a), 820.3); it keeps FDA scope and definitions (820.1, 820.3) and adds FDA requirements in 820.10(b)-(e), 820.35 and 820.45; the former QS regulation's Subparts C-O were removed and reserved (820.20-820.30 and 820.40 reserved); QS-regulation record-type terms such as DMR, DHR and DHF were eliminated; and Part 4 was conformed. Effective (and compliance required from) February 2, 2026. ISO scope: ISO 13485:2016 in its entirety, including the Introduction.

question_interpretation: Asks whether Part 820 requires ISO 13485 certification and whether a certificate exempts a manufacturer from FDA inspection.

issues.detail: 820.1(c) (Foreign manufacturers) concerns refusal of admission of imported devices that appear adulterated; it says nothing about certification or exemption from inspection. It does not govern either part of the question.

The 'no exemption from inspection' element rests on non-codified preamble statements (89 FR 7518-7519, Comments 79-81) and FDA's inspection authority under FD&C Act section 704 (21 U.S.C. 374), which is unaffected by the rule. No regulatory text in Part 820 addresses certificates. The key should say so rather than cite 820.1(c).
Clause 4.1 is corroborated as part of FDA's 'General requirements' grouping (21 CFR 4.4(b)(1)(i)); Clause 1 'Scope' is not named in any FDA text located.

explanation: J is correct: Part 820 contains no certification requirement (820.10(a) requires a documented QMS that complies with ISO 13485), and FDA states it will not require certification and that certificate holders are not exempt from FDA inspection. G's 820.1(c) is not a governing provision for either point. A correct answer would cite 820.10(a), the preamble and FD&C Act 704, and would not match it. H's Clause 1 is unverified.
proposed_corrected_answer: No. Part 820 imposes no ISO 13485 certification requirement; 820.10(a) requires the manufacturer to document a QMS that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485 and the rest of Part 820. A certificate does not exempt the manufacturer from FDA inspection. FDA said in the QMSR preamble that it will not require or rely on ISO 13485 certificates and that certificate holders are not exempt from inspection, and its inspection authority under FD&C Act section 704 is unaffected. These are preamble statements and statutory authority, not Part 820 regulatory text.
proposed_sections: 21 CFR 820.10(a); QMSR final rule preamble, 89 FR 7518-7519 (Comments 79-81); FD&C Act section 704 (21 U.S.C. 374)

question_interpretation: Asks which Title 21 parts govern establishment registration, device listing and UDI, and how they interact with Part 820.

issues.detail: UDI is governed by part 830 and by part 801 subpart B (801.20: label and package must bear a UDI meeting subpart B and part 830; 801.45 direct marking). G/J omit part 801 subpart B.

Other Part 820 touchpoints for UDI: 820.35(a)(3) and 820.35(b)(2) (any UDI/UPC recorded in complaint and servicing records) and 820.45(a)(1) (labeling examined for the correct UDI/UPC). J mentions only 820.10(b)(1) and 820.35(c).

J does not address how Part 807 interacts with Part 820. Part 820 contains no reference to part 807 and part 807 none to part 820; the honest answer is that they are separate obligations with overlapping 'manufacturer' coverage, and no cross-reference exists.

explanation: Part 807 (registration and listing) and Part 830 (UDI system and GUDID) are correctly identified, as are 820.10(b)(1) (documented UDI-assignment system per part 830, for Clause 7.5.8) and 820.35(c) (UDI recorded per device or batch). The key omits the part 801 subpart B labeling requirement to bear a UDI and Part 820's other UDI provisions. It also does not answer the Part 807 half of 'how do they interact'. H (7.5.8; 7.5.9) is named in 820.10(b) and 820.35(c).
proposed_corrected_answer: Registration and listing: 21 CFR part 807 (e.g., 807.20). UDI: 21 CFR part 830 (UDI requirements, issuing agencies, GUDID) and part 801 subpart B (801.20 label/package must bear a UDI; 801.45 direct marking). Interaction with Part 820: 820.10(b)(1) requires a documented system to assign UDIs per part 830 (Clause 7.5.8); 820.35(c) requires the UDI to be recorded for each device or batch (Clauses 7.5.1, 7.5.8, 7.5.9); 820.35(a)(3) and (b)(2) require any UDI/UPC in complaint and servicing records; 820.45(a)(1) requires labeling to be examined for the correct UDI/UPC. Part 820 does not cross-reference part 807; registration/listing is a separate obligation.
